tasks.title: Find the Funnel Bottleneck
tasks.context: 10,000 visitors create 2,500 product views, 1,000 carts and 400 purchases.
tasks.goal: Identify the stage transition with the lowest conversion.
tasks.prompt: Which transition has the lowest conversion rate?
tasks.explanation: Funnel analysis compares adjacent stage conversion, not just raw counts.

tasks.title: Interpret Cohort Retention
tasks.context: January cohort retains 62% at month 3; February retains 71% at month 3.
tasks.goal: Interpret the cohort comparison without overclaiming.
tasks.expectedAnswer: February shows higher month-3 retention, but cohort size and acquisition mix should be checked before attributing the improvement to product changes.
hints: Retention alone does not reveal cause.
tasks.explanation: Cohorts make lifecycle comparisons fairer, but causal interpretation still needs context.
options: February shows higher month-3 retention, but cohort size and acquisition mix should be checked before attributing the improvement to product changes.
February proves the product change caused 9 points of retention lift.
January should be excluded because it is older.

tasks.title: Calculate CAC
tasks.context: Marketing spent ₹300,000 and acquired 150 new paying customers.
tasks.deliverable: Enter the formula using B2=spend and C2=new customers.
tasks.prompt: Write CAC = acquisition spend / new customers.
hints: CAC is cost per acquired customer.
tasks.explanation: CAC normalizes acquisition spend by the number of new customers acquired.

tasks.title: Estimate Simple LTV
tasks.context: Average monthly gross profit per customer is ₹1,200 and average lifetime is 18 months.
tasks.deliverable: Enter gross profit per month × lifetime.
tasks.prompt: If B2 is monthly gross profit and C2 is lifetime months, write simple LTV.
hints: This is a simplified LTV model.
tasks.explanation: Simple LTV is useful for intuition but real models should consider retention curves, discounting and contribution margin.

tasks.title: CAC Payback Period
tasks.context: CAC is ₹18,000 and monthly gross profit per customer is ₹1,500.
tasks.goal: Calculate months to recover acquisition cost.
tasks.prompt: If B2 is CAC and C2 is monthly gross profit, write payback months.
hints: Payback asks how many months recover CAC.
Monthly gross profit is the denominator.
tasks.explanation: CAC payback translates acquisition economics into a cash-recovery horizon.

tasks.title: Interpret Net Revenue Retention
tasks.context: Starting MRR is ₹1,000,000; expansion is ₹120,000; contraction is ₹50,000; churn is ₹70,000.
hints: Add expansion, subtract contraction and churn.
Divide ending retained/expanded MRR by starting MRR.
tasks.explanation: NRR = (starting MRR + expansion - contraction - churn) / starting MRR.

tasks.title: Choose a Simple Forecast
tasks.context: Weekly shipments are 420, 450, 480 and 510 with no known structural change; planners need a simple transparent baseline.
tasks.goal: Choose an appropriate simple forecasting baseline.
tasks.prompt: What should the analyst use first?
tasks.expectedAnswer: A recent moving average or simple trend baseline, then back-test forecast error before using it for capacity decisions.
hints: Forecasts should include error, not just a point estimate.
tasks.explanation: Simple baselines are valuable benchmarks; complex models should beat them out of sample before deployment.
options: A recent moving average or simple trend baseline, then back-test forecast error before using it for capacity decisions.
Use the single highest week as every future forecast.
Assume the next week is exactly 510 because the last week was 510.
